title: Authorized-Unit Ledger Rules for Referrals & Prior Authorizations
content:
Every Referrals & Prior Authorizations case keeps a ledger of authorized units: the units of service the referral or authorization still covers. Grants and restorations add units; completed visits and lapses remove them. One unit is one of the type's unit measure — a visit, a study or a procedure.

## Clauses on granting units

- **Retired clause, no longer in force:** the clause under which an initial or appeal approval grants the type's units per approval, an extension grants the type's extension units (none where that figure is zero), and a retroactive authorization grants exactly the units of the services it covers. This clause has been superseded by the current basis and no longer governs a grant.
- **Retired clause, no longer in force:** the clause that units are granted only when the referral status is approved. This clause has been superseded by the current basis and no longer governs a grant.

## Clauses on using units (in force)

1. Each completed in-person visit booked against the referral uses one unit. A completed telehealth visit with the rendering provider uses one unit only where the type counts telehealth visits against units.
2. A unit is used only while the referral status is approved and the date of the visit is within the first date of validity to the valid-through date, as the referral record shows them. A visit that is cancelled or missed uses nothing.
3. Where the type's weekly cap is above zero, the units used in one calendar week may not exceed it, and a visit beyond the weekly cap is not covered by the authorization. The units of a week are the units used on the referral by visits dated in the Monday-to-Sunday week that contains the visit, less the units restored that reverse those uses. A visit is within the cap when the type has no weekly cap or when the week's units before it are fewer than the cap.
4. When the units remaining reach zero, the referral becomes exhausted.
5. Coverage is re-verified before a unit is used whenever the last verification is older than the type's re-verification figure, and where the type's progress-note figure is above zero a progress note goes to the payer after every that many units.

## Clauses on restoring a unit (in force)

6. A unit counted in error — a visit not rendered, a duplicate posting, or a use on the wrong referral — is restored when the correction is asked for in time.
7. The restoration is requested no later than the type's restore window counted from the date the unit was used, as that date stands on the unit-use entry of the ledger. The window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the unit date, and a request on the last day still qualifies.
8. A unit-use entry is restored at most once.
9. Restoring a unit on an exhausted referral returns it to approved only through an extension decision; otherwise the restored unit is usable only while the referral is approved.

## Weekly cap illustration (hypothetical weekly cap of 3)

| Visit in one Monday-to-Sunday week | Units already used that week | Within the cap |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | 0 | yes |
| Wednesday | 1 | yes |
| Friday | 2 | yes |
| Saturday | 3 | no — not covered by the authorization |

## Restore window boundaries (hypothetical unit dates)

| Restore window | Unit used on | Last day a request qualifies | Request on | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30 days | 2026-03-02 | 2026-04-01 | 2026-04-01 | in time |
| 30 days | 2026-03-02 | 2026-04-01 | 2026-04-02 | too late |
| 14 days | 2026-03-02 | 2026-03-16 | 2026-03-16 | in time |
| 14 days | 2026-03-02 | 2026-03-16 | 2026-03-17 | too late |

Day 1 of each window is 3 March, the day after the unit date.

superseded_clauses: An initial or appeal approval grants the tier's units_per_approval, an extension grants extension_units (none where that is 0), and a retroactive authorization grants exactly the units of the services it covers.
Units are granted only when the referral status is approved.
